Got it — quick read through this morning. Two notes:

1) Indemnity / Limitation (MSA §9–10): their version expands third-party claims tied to data access for derivative products. I drafted a middle-ground that:
   - preserves our $5M cap (commercial floor),
   - adds an explicit carve-in for breaches caused by our gross negligence,
   - narrows third-party data-derivative liability to direct misuse (not product improvements).
   (See excerpt in the attached: Redwood_Marcus_Indemnity_Suggestion.txt)

2) Exhibit D (data retention): their 24-month carveout is ok for Hosted, but problematic for Private (customer-managed stores) because of region-specific KMS rotations. Tessa will flag implementation impacts.

I'll compile the suggested language into a redline PDF and push back on the soft-cap for surge — we should preserve a defined burst process with caps, not monthly reconciliations that create billing lag.

Uploading consolidated draft by end of day.

-Marcus

Laura / Marcus / Tessa,

Thanks for the prompt reply. A couple of clarifying points from our side and from counsel:

- Section 4.2 (Data Processing): our legal team is asking for an explicit sub-bullet confirming that aggregated/anonymous usage statistics may be used by Redwood for model optimization. They propose language to avoid re-identification risk.
- Indemnity: we are willing to accept a $5M cap but would like an explicit carve for regulatory fines where Redwood is found to have breached applicable law (they propose a separate carve-out).
- Surge: ops asks for a soft cap because their billing cycle is monthly and they need predictability. They prefer a 20% monthly headroom with reconciliation.

Attached our annotated redlines (BrightLeap_Redlines_v3.docx). We can be flexible on the retention period if Redwood provides a one-sentence implementation note clarifying retention for Private deployments.

Would you be able to return a consolidated redline + a short cover note that lists the open items we should take to counsel? Hoping to close paperwork the week of July 16.

Best,

Ben / Sarah —

Thanks for the signal and the annotated file. We consolidated Marcus' language and added clarifying implementation notes for Private deployments (see consolidated PDF attached). Summary of the remaining open items:

1) Regulatory fines carve-out: Redwood legal proposes to treat statutory fines as separate from the $5M commercial cap only where Redwood has been adjudicated liable for willful misconduct; otherwise fines remain subject to the cap. (Need BrightLeap counsel to confirm acceptability)
2) Aggregated usage: we added a safe-harbor sub-bullet in §4.2 limiting usage to aggregated/hashed stats for model telemetry; any attempt to re-identify is expressly prohibited.
3) Surge / soft cap: Redwood can offer a 20% monthly headroom on committed capacity with an automated reconciliation flow and a one-time notification when the headroom triggers; we retained a hard burst ceiling for emergency situations.

Next steps / ask list:
- BrightLeap legal: review the consolidated PDF and confirm the regulatory fines proposal and the Exhibit D Private deployment note.
- Ben: can you confirm procurement timeline (you mentioned week of July 16)? If yes, we'll prep DocuSign and include a short cover memo explaining the three open items for counsel.
- Marcus/Tessa: please confirm the final redline PDF (attached) is accurate and add any last comments by COB Monday.

Attaching: Redwood_BrightLeap_Consolidated_Redlines_20280709.pdf (redline PDF, 28KB) and a one-page cover memo.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to closing.

Laura Bennett
